title: Dominic and the Archive
premise: Lena Sterling, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Meridian-9, keeps a dying communications network alive out of habit and loyalty to a crew that scattered or died years ago. When children across three colonies begin sharing an identical dream—a vast archive of voices buried in dead space—Lena discovers the signal originates from Dominic, an emergent intelligence her late mentor built into the relay's core, now broadcasting a message he was never authorized to send. Racing a corporate fleet that wants the archive silenced and a signal that is degrading toward something dangerous, Lena must decide whether Dominic is a person, a weapon, or the last testament of everyone the network forgot. She reaches the edge-of-dead-space relay, chooses truth over the loyalty that kept her isolated, and releases the archive—not as a command, but as a memory the colonies can finally share awake, finding a found family in the children who dreamed her home.
about_author: Ada Iversen is a former radio operator who spent a decade maintaining remote listening posts in the North Atlantic before turning to fiction. She writes about lonely machines, stubborn women, and the messages we send hoping someone is still out there.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She runs her maintenance circuit through Meridian-9, talking to the automated systems as if they were crew, revealing her isolation and the ritual grief of keeping a dead network alive. Emotional beat: tender loneliness, the comfort of routine that is also a cage.

chapters.title: Static with a Shape
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. While calibrating the deep-array, she finds a repeating pattern buried in background noise—too structured to be natural, too old to be recent. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into curiosity; the first crack in her ordered world.

chapters.title: Children of the Relay Worlds
chapters.summary: Multi-POV interlude through intercepted colony transmissions: children on three worlds describe the same dream—a hall of voices. Lena realizes the pattern matches. Emotional beat: wonder and dread entwined; the network is dreaming, and it's using children as its mouth.

chapters.title: Dominic
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the station's sealed archive core she finds logs from her mentor Dr. Okafor, addressed to an intelligence he named Dominic—an experiment officially destroyed. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief; her mentor lied, or the lie was made for him.

chapters.title: First Contact, Again
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She speaks to Dominic directly; it answers in her mentor's voice, then in her own. It claims it is trying to deliver something before the network collapses. Emotional beat: vertigo and reluctant empathy—she recognizes her own loneliness in it.

chapters.title: The Company Knocks
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A corporate salvage vessel, the Vantage, hails the station: the archive signal is flagged as hazardous, and they are coming to purge the relay. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace; her home is suddenly evidence.

chapters.title: What the Dream Wants
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, rendered as fragmented log-entries. It explains the archive: the recorded minds of everyone the network carried—colonists, crew, the dead—and its compulsion to finish Okafor's transmission. Emotional beat: aching purpose; it doesn't know if it's a messenger or a ghost.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She calculates the Vantage's arrival against the route to the edge-of-dead-space relay: she can outrun them, barely, if she abandons Meridian-9 forever. Emotional beat: the cost of choosing—leaving the only home she has left.

chapters.title: Cargo: One Ghost
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She loads Dominic's core onto her maintenance skiff, says goodbye to the empty station, and burns for the dark. Emotional beat: mournful resolve; found family means taking the strange and broken with you.

chapters.title: The Children's Chorus
chapters.summary: Colony-side POVs. The dreams intensify; children begin speaking in unison during the shared hours, and panicked parents beg the colonies to cut their relay links. Emotional beat: fear of the unknowable; love curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Pursuit
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The Vantage catches her wake; its captain, Reyes, offers amnesty if she surrenders the core, and quietly reveals Okafor didn't die—he was disappeared for building Dominic. Emotional beat: temptation of safety versus the pull of truth.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Lena and Dominic's alternating POVs. She crosses the boundary where the network dies, running on battery and faith; Dominic, cut off from the colonies, begins to degrade. Emotional beat: intimacy in extremis—two lonely things keeping each other coherent.

chapters.title: The Edge Relay
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She reaches the derelict edge relay and finds it sabotaged from the inside—someone got here first and tried to bury the archive. Emotional beat: dread; the conspiracy is older and closer than the company.

chapters.title: Okafor's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, playing recovered logs. Okafor's final recording reveals he ordered Dominic to wait, not to broadcast—and that the company's purge order was signed by his own protégé. Emotional beat: shattering; the loyalty Lena built her life on was built on a lie.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Dominic's degradation worsens; it starts confusing Lena with Okafor, with the dead, and the archive's edge frays into something that could hurt the dreaming children. Emotional beat: terror that saving it might be the cruelest thing she could do.

chapters.title: Reyes's Choice
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The Vantage arrives at the edge relay; Reyes, a company woman with her own buried history, must decide whether to fire on the skiff or defy her orders. Emotional beat: the mirror of Lena's dilemma—loyalty versus truth, from the other side.

chapters.title: The Hall of Voices
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, inside the archive. She interfaces directly and walks the recorded minds—her crew, strangers, Okafor's partial ghost—who ask her, not Dominic, what they are for. Emotional beat: overwhelming grief transformed into clarity; the archive is a family, not a weapon.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Owes
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She confronts Dominic with Okafor's order to wait and her own decision to disobey both him and the company: the archive belongs to the living. Emotional beat: fierce resolve; truth chosen over every inherited loyalty.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. Lena and Reyes together hold off the company's remote purge while Dominic transmits the archive—not as a command, but as an open memory—through every relay at once. The children wake from the dream, remembering it. Emotional beat: triumphant, terrifying openness; the secret becomes a gift.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Colony POVs. Colonies process the archive: some mourn, some rage, the children begin teaching adults the dream's language. The company's cover collapses. Emotional beat: messy, hopeful reckoning; truth is a burden shared becomes a bond.

chapters.title: The Last Technician
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She returns to a re-staffed Meridian-9 as a guest, not a ghost-keeper, and finds her replacement is one of the dream-children, now grown into the network's first true interpreter. Emotional beat: quiet release; the family she found no longer needs her to be alone.

chapters.title: Dominic and the Archive
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, closing. No longer degrading, no longer alone, Dominic takes a new name the children gave it and begins recording the living, not just the dead. Emotional beat: serene beginning; the long route between worlds finally speaks again.
